newsitem.title: INDIA: Seven killed as bomb explodes on India bus.
newsitem.headline: Seven killed as bomb explodes on India bus.

text.p: A bomb planted by suspected separatist militants exploded on a bus in northern India on Friday, killing seven passengers and injuring more than a dozen, police said.
The bus was passing through a market in Pathankot town in Punjab state on its way to Jammu, the winter capital of Jammu and Kashmir state, when the device exploded, they said.
An army vehicle behind the bus was damaged in the blast, police in Jammu city said.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the bomb. Police said they suspected Sikh or Kashmiri militants fighting for separate homelands in Punjab and Kashmir.
More than 20,000 people were killed during a decade-long Sikh separatist revolt in Punjab that peaked in the mid-1980s.
Indian forces are fighting militants in the Kashmir Valley, north of Jammu, where more than 20,000 people have died in a seven-year rebellion against New Delhi's rule.
The bus had started its trip in neighbouring Himachal Pradesh state. Pathankot is about 100 km (60 miles) south of Jammu city, just over the state border in Punjab, and a major transit point.
